 Texas A&M expert discusses changes to federal student loans 
 Texas A&M expert discusses changes to federal student loans By Luke Galindo Published : Nov. 13, 2026 at 8:22 PM CST | Updated : 13 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLLEGE STATION, Texas (KBTX) - Changes to federal student loans include new borrowing limits that could affect students pursuing graduate degrees, according to a Texas A&M University expert.
 Lori Taylor, head of the Department of Public Service and Administration at Texas A&M’s Bush School of Government and Public Service, said the One Big Beautiful Bill Act eliminated an existing loan program that allowed graduate students to borrow additional funds without a set limit.
 New borrowing limits
 Taylor said the new rules set annual and lifetime limits on federal borrowing, with different limits depending on the type of program. She said the annual limit for a master’s program is a little more than $20,000.
 That could have a substantial effect on students in programs where tuition exceeds the annual limit, Taylor said. She also raised concerns about access to loans for low-income households and about which programs qualify as professional programs.
 College costs and student choices
 Taylor said rising tuition and the cost of living can put pressure on students who rely on loans. She said prospective students may need to consider a school’s cost of attendance and living expenses when choosing a program.
 Taylor said the borrowing limits could make Texas A&M more cost competitive. She also said more graduate students are working while in school, which she believes can affect their collegiate experience.
